gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy any candidate actually delivered in a named lab's discharge test. StorageReview measured 2.39 kWh from the BLUETTI Apex 300 (86% of 2,764.8 Wh), 7.38 kWh from the Apex 300 with two B300K packs (89%) and 3.07 kWh from the Elite 400 (80% of 3,840 Wh). OutdoorGearLab measured 3,790 Wh from the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (over 93% of 4,096 Wh).
standout_why: I compared against three StormWatts pages. The cited 'kits compared at the same panel watts' page (2026-11-08, updated 11-12) says 'We have not tested these products hands-on' and gives only spec Wh and its own arithmetic. Its only measured number is the site owner's 696 W solar peak on a Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus, which is not a candidate. The '5 kWh-class solar input' page (2026-11-16) says 'Nothing on this page comes from hands-on testing.' The ShopSolar result (Anker F3800 page) and ChatGPT's answer use only rated capacity. I could not open two cited pages: theoutageready.com gave an SSL certificate error and solargenreview.com returned HTTP 429. So I can't rule out a measurement there, though ChatGPT's answer quoted none. Nothing I opened compares delivered energy, round-trip efficiency or UPS switchover times.
decides: The measurements change the value order among the BLUETTI kits we link and widen the gap to the rival flagship. Measured on the same blower-fan method, the Elite 400 delivered 3.07 kWh and the Apex 300 2.39 kWh. That puts the Elite 400 + 2× 200 W kit at about $0.59 per delivered Wh ($1,804.05 / 3,070 Wh), against about $0.87 for the Apex 300 + 2× 200 W ($2,089.05 / 2,390 Wh). The Apex 300 + 2× B300K + 2× 200 W kit comes to about $0.59 per delivered Wh ($4,369.05 / 7,380 Wh), the most delivered energy under $5,000. Against the rival flagship, the DELTA Pro 3 is rated only 256 Wh above the Elite 400, but the measured gap is about 660–720 Wh (3,790 OutdoorGearLab or about 3,700 Digital Trends, against 3,070 StorageReview). These come from different labs and methods, so the gap is an indication, not an exact figure. This does not change which kit is the ships-now pick. Every kit with a named measurement is a pre-order: the Elite 400 kits dispatch mid-to-late December 2026 and the Apex 300 kits late January 2027. The ships-now kits we link (BLUETTI 5kWh RV kits, ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP037/SP039) have no named lab measurement I could find. The figures belong as context for the 'cheaper or larger if you can wait' option and against the rivals. Dealectric does not test units.
